verdicts.note: Expert consensus on improving ART access across ASIA PACIFIC — a region absent from the rest of the frame, and where the very-low-fertility settings are.
Anthropology of infertility in Africa. Wall 8.
Global infertility prevalence from 277 surveys. Wall 4, and the standard citation for the size of the treatable population.
Semen parameters in fertile vs infertile men.
NCHS data brief on delayed childbearing.
Phthalates and sperm DNA damage. B.2/B.6's.

**PREDICTION RULES FOR SPONTANEOUS PREGNANCY leading to live birth among subfertile couples.** The counterfactual made operational: a model that says, for a given couple, how likely a live birth is WITHOUT treatment. Seventh record in this family and the most directly usable — it converts the upper-bound argument into a subtractable quantity.
No abstract. Clinical review of delayed childbearing.
Mean age of mother 1970-2000, NCHS.
Meta-synthesis of women's reasoning about advanced maternal age — 'informed and uninformed decision making' is P6's distinction in qualitative form.

**Cumulative live-birth rates across complete cycles, 178,898 linked women.** The conversion rate from entering treatment to a birth, at population scale. Per-couple rather than per-cycle, which is the denominator arm 1 needs; Wall 1 by outcome type but load-bearing for the recovery arithmetic.
Terminology proposal.
No abstract. Racial disparities in ART outcomes over time.
Ottawa students' awareness of infertility risk and ART.

**GEOGRAPHIC ACCESS to ART across the United States, population-based.** The distance margin measured nationally rather than in one health system — the strongest P2 exposure record in the frame alongside the Australian proximity study.
No abstract; title is a direct statement of arm 2's question — will DECREASING COSTS improve utilisation and outcomes among minority women.
Serum estradiol and frozen-transfer outcomes.
Measuring sterility from incomplete birth histories. Methods for the PM/FDT literature.
Faculty work-life balance.
Socio-economic disparities in ART access in AUSTRALIA — the setting with the most policy variation in the frame (2010 Medicare cut, the consumer-cost rise, the SET funding regime).
Fertility-information app for male cancer patients.
Preprint of the same app usability study.
Polemic defending single-embryo transfer. A.12's policy debate.

Preservation for a transgender teenager. **Second gender-affirming case in the frame and again Wall 5's binary has no home for it** — recorded as `neither` because neither onco nor elective is the right label.
Population trends in ART multiple gestation.

**REGULATION of MAR — public funding and single-embryo-transfer rules — against infant hospitalisation.** An A.17 exposure (funding) and an A.12 lever (SET) producing a Wall 2 outcome. A three-way boundary case; route to A.12 with a flag and note the funding arm for P1.

**Scoping review of fertility needs before and after oocyte freezing, EXPLICITLY SPLIT BY MEDICAL AND NON-MEDICAL REASONS.** The only record in the frame that draws Wall 5's own distinction and reports both sides. Use it to calibrate the indication split rather than relying on the term-matcher.
Preservation counselling referral in cancer patients.
Fertility management after pituitary surgery, case report.
Barriers to preservation discussion in young women with cancer.
Oncofertility care for children and young adults.
Japanese male-infertility clinical guidelines, framed against the declining birth rate.
Preservation as a cancer survivorship issue.
Financial assistance programme for preservation in young cancer patients. An access exposure inside Wall 5's medical half — the same shape as the FP mandates, and out for the same reason.
Preservation counselling before chemotherapy.
Preservation referral patterns in breast cancer.
Neuro-oncology preservation SR protocol.
Preprint of the same protocol.
Infertility and adverse pregnancy outcomes. Note its design: it compares women who conceived WITHOUT treatment after long time-to-pregnancy — the untreated-subfertile comparison group again.
Male preservation in oncology.

**The BELGIAN project — reimbursement tied to embryo-transfer limits.** Belgium's 2003 reform is the textbook case where FUNDING was made conditional on SET, so an A.17 exposure and an A.12 lever were bundled by design. Route to A.12, flag for P1: the two chapters cannot cleanly separate this policy and should say so.
Fertility optimisation in women with cancer.
Letrozole vs HRT endometrial preparation.
LIVE BIRTH after cancer in 63,000 young patients, with racial inequities. A birth outcome, but the population is Wall 5's medical half.
ICMART world report 2004.
ART and birth defects across three states.
Lifestyle risk factors for poor semen quality.
Overview of US fertility treatments tied to the National Public Health Action Plan.
Early pregnancy loss, India. B.5's.
Argument for preservation coverage in breast cancer.

**'IVF AND SPONTANEOUS PREGNANCIES: MATCHING OUTCOMES', Douala, Cameroon.** An explicit matched comparison of treated and spontaneously conceiving couples. Non-OECD so it tags SECONDARY under Wall 8, but the DESIGN is the one arm 1's counterfactual needs and almost nothing in the OECD frame supplies.
Infertility services for US Veterans — a distinct coverage regime (VA) outside both state mandates and employer plans.
Ovulatory-cycle frozen transfer protocol.
Preservation outcomes in Iranian cancer patients.
CDC ART Surveillance 2018 — the latest US edition in the frame.
CDC ART Surveillance 2017.
ART and autism in California.
Survey of national oncofertility registries.
Time to pregnancy and infant neurological condition.
Fertility treatment and childhood cancer risk.
